source_audit: 75 photographs (v2 library + 30 generic-business additions), each visually inspected and measured. 45 photographs (v2 library — REPLACES the v1 set entirely), each visually inspected and measured.

selection_contract.customer_photo_wins: A customer-supplied Image URL or upload disables stock selection entirely.
selection_contract.industry_match: HARD GATE on depicts[] only — what the photograph actually shows. A specific trade never receives a broad-category or lifestyle photo: matching resolves to the most specific tier that has a depicting photo and never widens past it. No nearest-neighbour fallback; an unmatched industry means no photo.
selection_contract.orientation_rule: The photograph's orientation does NOT have to match the product's. The photo is composed INTO the design via its suitable_roles — a portrait file becomes a vertical side panel, tall inset or vertical hero on a landscape product; a landscape file a horizontal band on a portrait one. The prompt carries the roles; the model builds a compatible photo area around the file.
selection_contract.text_safety: Important text must not sit on a region graded poor unless overlay_guidance.scrim_opacity_if_used is applied.
selection_contract.suppresses: When a photo is placed, design-asset usage drops to at most one quiet texture or frame.
selection_contract.audit_associations: Provenance from the Phase 2C audit. NEVER used to select — it is what allowed a family-in-a-park photo to answer "dentist".
selection_contract.known_industries: The full trade vocabulary the matcher understands. A slug here with no depicting photograph is a recognised SPECIFIC trade that the library cannot serve — naming it yields no photo, and never a broad-category substitute.
selection_contract.general_purpose: Photos flagged general_purpose are industry-neutral — neutral professional people, generic workspace, neutral architecture/interiors, broad lifestyle, nature. They are the ONLY photos reachable when no industry can be determined from the brief; a specific trade photo is never a fallback.
